references.disposition: A single N_ε independent of x is the defining uniform-convergence quantifier condition.
The eventual distance bound for every x is the defining metric uniform-convergence inequality.
All domain points are quantified after the existence of a single N for each epsilon.

references.phrase: differentiable at every point of I
references.disposition: Single-point derivatives existing throughout I is the domain requirement for the derivative function being defined.
The derivative-value assignment is precisely the derivative function being defined, not a distinct prerequisite.

references.phrase: derivative function distinct from derivative at one point
references.disposition: The domain of f′ consists of every point in I and presupposes differentiability at each.
